source_ip.label: Source IP Address
source_ip.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Source IP

From active firewall sessions:
  show conn
    Left column = source IP of active connections
  show conn | in <keyword>
    Filter to find specific sessions

From firewall logs:
  show logging | in <keyword>
    Syslog shows source IP of denied/permitted traffic
  show logging | in Deny
    All denied traffic with source IPs

From customer ticket:
  Customer provides source server IP or hostname.
  Resolve hostname: nslookup <hostname>

Common usage:
  packet-tracer input <IF> tcp <SOURCE_IP> 12345 <DST> 443
  access-list <ACL> extended permit ip host <SOURCE_IP> host <DST>
  shun <SOURCE_IP>   [immediate block]
  show conn | in <SOURCE_IP>

dest_ip.label: Destination IP Address
dest_ip.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Destination IP

Identify destination interface/subnet:
  show nameif
    Lists all interface names with their security levels
    Match subnet to interface (e.g. HYP-INFRA -> 172.24.128.0/22)
  show interface ip brief
    All interface IPs — destination may be directly connected

Verify route to destination:
  show route <DEST_IP>
    Confirms destination is reachable
    Shows which interface and next-hop

For NAT environments:
  show run nat | in <DEST_IP>
    Shows translated address
  show xlate | in <DEST_IP>
    Shows active translations

For F5:
  show ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
    Shows VIP destination IP:PORT

Common usage:
  packet-tracer input <IF> tcp <SRC> 12345 <DEST_IP> 443
  show conn | in <DEST_IP>
  show route <DEST_IP>

interface.label: Interface / Zone Name
interface.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Interface / Zone Name

Cisco ASA / Firepower:
  show nameif
    Lists ALL logical interface names (outside, inside, DMZ, DEV, HYP-INFRA)
    Shows IP address and security level for each
    MOST RELIABLE method — match your source/dest subnet here
  show interface ip brief
    All interfaces with IP and state (up/down)
  show run access-group
    Shows which ACL name is applied on which interface
    Format: access-group <ACL_NAME> in interface <INTERFACE_NAME>

Example output from show nameif:
  Interface     Name     Security
  Gi0/0         outside  0
  Gi0/1         inside   100
  Gi0/2         DMZ      50
  Gi0/3         DEV      60

Common usage:
  packet-tracer input <INTERFACE> tcp ...
  access-group <ACL> in interface <INTERFACE>

port.label: Port Number
port.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Port Number

From active connections:
  show conn
    Format: TCP <SRC_IP>:<SRC_PORT> <DST_IP>:<DST_PORT>
  show conn | in <IP_ADDRESS>
    Filter to find ports for specific IP

From firewall logs:
  show logging | in <IP_ADDRESS>
    Shows port numbers in dropped/permitted traffic

Common well-known ports:
  HTTPS  = 443      HTTP   = 80
  SSH    = 22       RDP    = 3389
  FTP    = 21       SMTP   = 25
  DNS    = 53       SNMP   = 161
  MySQL  = 3306     MSSQL  = 1433
  IKE    = 500/4500 BGP    = 179
  LDAP   = 389      LDAPS  = 636
  NTP    = 123      RADIUS = 1812

Common usage:
  packet-tracer input <IF> tcp <SRC> 12345 <DST> <PORT>
  access-list <ACL> extended permit tcp host <SRC> host <DST> eq <PORT>

acl_name.label: ACL Name / Number
acl_name.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — ACL Name or Number

Most reliable method:
  show run access-group
    Output format: access-group <ACL_NAME> in interface <INTERFACE>
    This shows EXACTLY which ACL is applied inbound on each interface
    ALWAYS check this first

Find all ACLs and hit counts:
  show access-list
    Lists ALL ACLs with current hit counts
    High hit count = traffic is matching that rule
  show run | in access-list
    Search running config for access-list entries

Find ACL on specific interface:
  show run interface <INTERFACE_NAME>
    Look for: ip access-group <ACL_NAME> in

Common naming patterns:
  101, 102        = numbered ACLs (legacy Cisco)
  OUTSIDE_IN      = inbound on outside interface
  INSIDE_IN       = inbound on inside interface
  VPN-ACL         = crypto ACL for site-to-site VPN
  VPN-FILTER      = VPN filter ACL in group-policy
  BLACKLIST_IPs   = IP blocking object-group referenced in deny rule

Common usage:
  show access-list <ACL_NAME>
  access-list <ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit ip ...
  no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended deny ...

device_id.label: Device ID
device_id.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Device ID

From ticketing system / CMDB:
  Device ID is assigned in CMDB (format: 7 digits e.g. 1309582)
  Check customer ticket — device IDs are usually listed
  Search Rackspace MyCloud portal by hostname or account

From the device itself:
  show version | in Hostname
    Get hostname then look up CMDB by hostname
  show version | in Serial
    Hardware serial number — look up in CMDB
  show inventory
    Full hardware inventory with serial numbers

NSCLI commands (uses Device ID):
  nscli zsp unlock <DEVICE_ID>     — elevate permissions
  nscli maint sweep -s <DEVICE_ID> — ping sweep
  nscli torq backup <DEVICE_ID>    — config backup
  nscli ssh <DEVICE_ID>            — SSH via jumphost
  nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>  — check permissions

vip_name.label: VIP / Virtual Server Name
vip_name.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — VIP / Virtual Server Name (F5)

List all virtual servers on F5:
  show ltm virtual
    Lists all VIPs with destination IP:PORT
    Look for the VIP matching your destination IP
  list ltm virtual
    Detailed config of all virtual servers

Find VIP by IP:
  show ltm virtual | in <IP_ADDRESS>
    Filter to find VIP for specific IP

VIP naming convention (Rackspace):
  VIP-<IP>-<PORT>     e.g. VIP-161.47.163.216-443
  VS-<IP>-<PORT>      e.g. VS-72.3.244.228-8080

Common usage:
  list ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
  show ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
  modify ltm virtual <VIP_NAME> ...

pool_name.label: Pool Name
pool_name.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — Pool Name (F5)

From the VIP configuration:
  list ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
    Shows the pool attribute — pool name is listed here
    Example: pool POOL_EIP_72.3.244.228-8080

List all pools directly:
  show ltm pool
    Lists all pools with member count and status
  list ltm pool
    Detailed config of all pools including members

Find pool by IP:
  show ltm pool | in <IP_ADDRESS>
    Find which pool contains a specific node IP

Pool naming convention (Rackspace):
  POOL_<NAME>-<PORT>  e.g. POOL_EIP_72.3.244.228-8080

Common usage:
  show ltm pool <POOL_NAME>
  list ltm pool <POOL_NAME>
  modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members add { <IP>:<PORT> }
  modify ltm pool <POOL_NAME> members modify { <IP>:<PORT> { session user-enabled }}

ssl_profile.label: SSL Profile Name
ssl_profile.tooltip:
HOW TO FIND — SSL Profile Name (F5)

From the VIP configuration:
  list ltm virtual <VIP_NAME>
    Look in 'profiles' section
    Find entry with 'context clientside' — that is the client-ssl profile
    Example: profiles { wildcard.itemworkshop.com { context clientside } }

List all client-ssl profiles:
  list ltm profile client-ssl
    Shows all SSL profiles with their cert/key assignments
  show ltm profile client-ssl <PROFILE_NAME>
    Status of a specific profile

Find profile by cert name:
  list ltm profile client-ssl | in <CERT_NAME>
    Filter to find which profile uses a specific certificate

Common naming convention (Rackspace):
  wildcard.<domain>    e.g. wildcard.itemworkshop.com
  <fqdn>-ssl          e.g. app.example.com-ssl

Common usage:
  list ltm profile client-ssl <SSL_PROFILE_NAME>
  modify ltm profile client-ssl <SSL_PROFILE_NAME> replace-all-with {...}
